why: Twelve translation teams of 8 to 71 translators earning $1 million to $13 million, roughly $125,000 to $185,000 of revenue per translator, is believable for a corporate translation firm.
A bottled water market of about €16.5 billion split into still, sparkling and a smaller fast-growing flavoured segment is believable for a large regional market.
162 hours a month per upholsterer, with half an upholsterer re-covering 50 chairs and 2.5 re-covering 233, works out at about 100 minutes per chair, which is believable.

Offices earning £15 million to £42 million in placement fees and spending £0.9 million to £4.6 million on job boards are high for single offices but within a factor of a few of what a large recruiter's main offices could report, and the fee-to-spend ratios are sensible.
A paddy-to-pack rice cost rising from €0.53 to €1.41 per kg, with the waterfall steps adding up exactly, is believable for a European rice packer.
An outlet village with 2 million visits from 900,000 shoppers in its first year, most of the repeat visitors coming about four times, is believable.

The sofa range's upholstery workshop cost of $12,400 cannot cover upholstering enough sofas for 197 to come back faulty: even if every sofa made were returned it is about $63 per sofa, and at any realistic fault rate a few dollars, far below what outsourced sofa upholstery costs and less than a third of the $192 per sofa spent on repairs.
36 jewellery stores taking about $2.7 million a month, roughly $900,000 a year per store with a December peak, is believable.
176 hours a month per framer, with half a framer making 46 frames and 2.5 making 215, works out at about two hours per custom frame, which is believable for a framing shop.
A toy maker shipping about 5 to 6 million toys a month at around $12 each, with profit equal to revenue minus costs and correct average month lengths, is believable.
